# [CS031] Secret Compared in Non-Constant Time (auth-non-constant-time-compare)

A secret such as a token, MAC or password hash is compared with == or bytes.Equal.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-208](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/208.html) |
| **OWASP** | A07:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

These comparisons stop at the first differing byte, so response timing reveals how much of a guess is correct. Use crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare or hmac.Equal.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
if r.Header.Get("X-Signature") == expectedSignature {
	process(r)
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
if hmac.Equal([]byte(r.Header.Get("X-Signature")), []byte(expectedSignature)) {
	process(r)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [auth-non-constant-time-compare]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    auth-non-constant-time-compare: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore auth-non-constant-time-compare -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** auth-non-constant-time-compare
```
